Done. Set up a new `payment-architecture-test` Maven module with ArchUnit that fails the build if:

1. **Domain** depends on application/infrastructure/app code.
2. **Application** depends on infrastructure/app code.
3. **Infrastructure** depends on the app wiring layer.
4. **Domain or application** code depends on any technical framework (`org.springframework..`, `com.fasterxml.jackson..`, `jakarta.servlet..`, `java.net.http..`) — this is the specific "technical detail leaking into business code" case you described.

I verified it by temporarily injecting a Spring `RestTemplate` field into the business-layer `AuthorizePayment` class — the build failed immediately with a precise violation report (constructor + field, file/line). Reverted afterward; repo is clean aside from the intended additions.

**On speed:** it's its own module, isolated from `payment-unit-test`. Your everyday save-loop (`mvn -pl payment-unit-test -am test`) timed identically before/after (~3s) since it never touches the new module. The architecture check only runs as part of the full `mvn test`/CI build (~7s total, ArchUnit itself ~2-5s of that).
